docRequirement: amazon-bedrock.md § "Use the Mantle endpoint" (line 433 of the .md): "Mantle is an Amazon Bedrock endpoint that serves Claude models through the native Anthropic API shape rather than the Amazon Bedrock Invoke API. It uses the same AWS credentials, IAM permissions, and `awsAuthRefresh` configuration described earlier on this page." Three env vars select it — `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE` (enable, `1` or `true`), `ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_MANTLE_BASE_URL` (override the endpoint URL), `CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_MANTLE_AUTH` (skip client-side auth for a gateway) — tabled at :495-497, and :460 states that setting `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK` and `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE` together lets one session call both endpoints. So the set of env vars that redirect a Claude Code process to Bedrock is six, not three: any code enforcing "Bedrock must never be routed through the Claude SDK path" is bound to all of them.
current: The sanitization mechanism exists and covers exactly the three Invoke-API vars. `buildClaudeSubprocessEnv` builds the Claude SDK subprocess env by spreading the whole ambient environment — `{...process.env, ...getProxyEnvVars(), ...envOverrides, NESSY_DEBUG}` (packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:239-245) — then deletes three keys under the comment "Bedrock must never be routed through the Claude SDK path" (options.ts:257-262): `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`, `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK`, `ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL`. That env feeds every spawn via `getDefaultOptions` (options.ts:276). The same three-key list is duplicated as `CLAUDE_BEDROCK_ROUTING_ENV_KEYS` (packages/shared/src/config/llm-connections.ts:931-935), wrapped by `clearClaudeBedrockRoutingEnvVars` (llm-connections.ts:969-975), which `ClaudeAgent.postInit` calls against the real `process.env` at packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:917 under "Claude subprocesses must never inherit Bedrock-routing toggles from a previous connection or parent process environment", and which is spread into `MANAGED_ANTHROPIC_AUTH_ENV_KEYS` (llm-connections.ts:941-950) so `resetManagedAnthropicAuthEnvVars` (llm-connections.ts:977-990) deletes rather than restores them (baseline forced to `undefined` at :959-967). `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE`, `ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_MANTLE_BASE_URL` and `CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_MANTLE_AUTH` appear nowhere in packages/, apps/ or scripts/ source (`grep -arn` over the tree hits only the doc-sweep artifacts under docs/superpowers/specs/ and the vendored `packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js:332857`, which is bundled SDK code, not ours), so all three survive the spread into the subprocess. The binary that receives them does honour them: `node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64/claude` (SDK pinned 0.3.183 by the `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` dependency entry of the root package.json, packages/shared/package.json and packages/core/package.json) contains `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE` 21 times, `ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_MANTLE_BASE_URL` 14 and `CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_MANTLE_AUTH` 14. A third, independent site has the same omission: the managed-settings classification table `MANAGED_ENV_CLASSIFICATION` (packages/shared/src/config/managed-env.ts:93-170) lists `ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK` and `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX` as `'routing'` (:123-126) and `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` as `'credential'` (:143), while `classifyManagedEnvVar` defaults every unlisted name to `'immediate'` (managed-env.ts:190-192) — so a server-cache managed `env` block carrying the three Mantle vars is applied at once by `resolveManagedEnv`/`applyManagedEnv` (managed-env.ts:255-259, 345-354) with no withhold-and-confirm gate, unlike its `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK` sibling. Nothing upstream compensates: our own Bedrock support runs through Pi's separate AWS path (`PiAgent.buildAwsEnv`, packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:2038-2061, sets only `AWS_*`), and packages/shared/AGENTS.md:37 documents the sanitization as the active invariant, naming the same three vars.
divergence: No key is misspelled and no value semantics are wrong — the delta is purely the membership of the routing-var lists. Two lists are short by the same three names (`CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE`, `ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_MANTLE_BASE_URL`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_MANTLE_AUTH`): options.ts:260-262 and `CLAUDE_BEDROCK_ROUTING_ENV_KEYS` at llm-connections.ts:931-935. A third list, `MANAGED_ENV_CLASSIFICATION` (managed-env.ts:93-170), classifies the same three as `'immediate'` by default omission when the doc makes two of them provider routing and one an auth switch — they should be `'routing'`/`'routing'`/`'credential'` to sit beside their Invoke-API siblings. Consequence of the delta, not part of it: the invariant the code states ("Bedrock must never be routed through the Claude SDK path") is satisfied for the Invoke API and defeated for Mantle, and the managed-settings consent surface withholds one half of a Bedrock configuration while applying the other silently. Same shape, wider: the bundled binary also honours `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX` (24 hits), `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY` (19), `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_ANTHROPIC_AWS` (21) with `ANTHROPIC_AWS_BASE_URL` (16), and `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_GATEWAY` (5), none of which the strip lists carry either — that overlap belongs to f118, and the fix below should be shaped as one shared provider-routing allowlist so it absorbs them rather than adding three more hardcoded deletes.

blastRadius: Every Claude SDK subprocess spawn: `buildClaudeSubprocessEnv` → `getDefaultOptions` (packages/shared/src/agent/options.ts:276). `ClaudeAgent.postInit` (packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:917) calls `clearClaudeBedrockRoutingEnvVars()` with no argument, i.e. against the host's real `process.env` — Electron main and the headless server — so growing the list widens a process-global mutation, not just a child env; anything else in that process reading `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE` would stop seeing it. `MANAGED_ANTHROPIC_AUTH_ENV_KEYS` (llm-connections.ts:941-950) spreads the constant, so `MANAGED_ANTHROPIC_AUTH_ENV_BASELINE` (:959-967) gains three keys whose baseline is forced `undefined` and `resetManagedAnthropicAuthEnvVars` (:977-990) will delete them — reached from `SessionManager.reinitializeAuth`, i.e. every connection switch. Tests that pin the current lists and will fail until updated: packages/shared/src/config/__tests__/managed-env.test.ts:34-56 (exact-set pin), packages/shared/src/config/__tests__/llm-connections-auth-env.test.ts:9-14 and :71-102, plus the prose assertion in packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/claude-turn-options.test.ts:58-62. Docs: packages/shared/AGENTS.md:37. No config-file field, RPC message or persisted schema changes — nothing is written to disk or the wire, so this is not a wire/schema risk trigger. It does touch two boundaries worth naming explicitly: (1) auth/permission-adjacent, since `CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_MANTLE_AUTH` is an authentication switch and `postInit` mutates the host process env — the repo's own risk-trigger list covers 'auth or permission decisions'; (2) the managed-settings consent surface, because `ManagedEnvResolutionV1.withheld` category members are what the withhold prompt lists, so moving a var from `'immediate'` to `'routing'`/`'credential'` changes what an administrator's cached `env` block shows the user (names only — the V1 shape itself is unchanged). Unaffected: the Pi path, which builds its own AWS env (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:2038-2061) and never sets a `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_*` flag.
userImpact: None observable for a default install — the vars have to be exported by the host shell (or arrive in a managed settings-cache `env` block) before anything changes. What makes it surface: a user on an AWS-integrated machine who has run the Mantle setup from Claude Code's own docs (`export CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE=1`, `export AWS_REGION=…`, or the gateway trio with `CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_MANTLE_AUTH=1` and `ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_MANTLE_BASE_URL=…`) and then launches Nessy from that shell and starts a session on any Claude connection. The subprocess inherits the flag and the bundled binary routes the turn to the Bedrock Mantle endpoint instead of the endpoint the connection card in Settings shows. Because Mantle needs `anthropic.`-prefixed model IDs while our connection sends a bare/versioned Claude ID, the visible result is a failing turn — a 4xx/model-not-found surfaced as a generic session error with no hint that the request left for AWS — or, with `CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_MANTLE_AUTH=1` and a gateway URL set, an unsigned request to the user's gateway host that appears to succeed while the configured connection was silently bypassed. The exact same shell state with `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK` instead produces no such effect, because that one is stripped; the asymmetry is what a user would experience as unexplainable. Second, narrower surface: an administrator's managed `env` block that sets Mantle is applied immediately with no withhold-and-confirm prompt, while the `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK` in the same block is held back and prompted — the consent dialog lists half the configuration it is protecting the user from.
